title: Provision Elastic IP
scenario: Your platform team needs Elastic IP for a static public IPv4 address. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_eip.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).
Tag the resource with Project, Environment and ManagedBy = "terraform".

focus.title: Complete the aws_eip resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_eip.

hints.why: A VPC is the network boundary for most AWS resources. CIDR planning, subnets and routing decisions affect everything deployed inside it.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_eip" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_eip. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Design a VPC when you need isolated networking, predictable address space or control over public and private traffic.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_eip" "this"`. Use this code shape: domain; instance; tags. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `aws_instance.this.id`, `var.project_name`, `var.environment`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
